newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway steps up monitoring of drilling rigs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Norway steps up monitoring of drilling rigs - paper.

text.p: Record high drilling activity on the Norwqegian continental shelf has led to the Norwegian Oil Directorate (OD) increasing its monitoring of rigs operating in Norwegian waters, the daily Stavanger Aftenblad said on Tuesday.

"We have stepped up our activity in line with what is taking place on the shelf. As more and more rigs begin to work, the chances of an accident increase," the newspaper quoted OD spokesman Jan Hagland as saying.
It said that the OD had followed drilling activity closely over the past year, particularly in the wells themselves.

Hagland emphasised that the OD had no grounds to believe that rigs from other areas were worse than those already in Norwegian territory. The OD expected all oil companies to follow regulations and safety procedures both for new and older rigs, he said.

Last week the OD served notice to Smedvig ASA to halt exploration drilling by the West Delta rig due to questions of adherence to maintenance and safety regulations. The rig was working for Norsk Hydro ASA.
Hagland said that because there was no oil pressure on the rig, there was no risk to worker safety.
"The purpose of the notice is to enter a dialogue with the operating companies. We must get answers to many questions before we come to any conclusions," Hagland told Stavanger Aftenblad.
"That Norsk Hydro and Smedvig are not fully agreed with all of our considerations is part of the investigation going on now."
He said the West Delta was being upgraded at sea. "We will see what happens when it tries to get new drilling permission in one week's time," Hagland said.
